ideas.title: Medicare's GLP-1 coverage change meets the Dec 7 open-enrollment deadline: what people on Part D actually need to check before picking a 2027 plan
ideas.beat: aging, body and metabolism / insurance policy
ideas.angle: Service journalism with a clock. A policy headline doesn't mean your plan covers the drug. Walk Medicare enrollees through how to check formulary status, prior-authorization and step-therapy rules, and the eligibility criteria (obesity vs. diabetes vs. cardiovascular indication) for semaglutide and tirzepatide in their 2027 Part D options before open enrollment closes Dec 7.
ideas.why_now: Medicare open enrollment runs through Dec 7, a real action window. The coverage change is reportedly a new development since early-November coverage, and readers who miss the window are locked into a plan for 2027.
ideas.is_it_real: The deadline is solid: Medicare's annual enrollment period ends Dec 7. The size and terms of the 'coverage expansion' are not verified in the input. The only sources are the CMS and Medicare.gov homepages, and the upstream fact-check is marked unverifiable. Before pitching, the exact 2027 Part D GLP-1 eligibility and coverage rules have to be confirmed from a specific CMS document. If the expansion turns out narrower or later than framed, the story shifts to 'what Medicare does and doesn't cover yet,' which still works with the deadline. Separate from the ACA open-enrollment pitch (Nov 2) and the compounded and counterfeit GLP-1 items.

notes: A thin day: all three terms came from the newsroom pipeline, and two are fixed calendar observances (World Diabetes Day, Great American Smokeout) with no news peg beyond the date, so neither clears the bar. The Medicare GLP-1 item is the only one with a real clock. Its underlying policy claim is unverified (homepage-only sources), so it is kept as a low-confidence pitch that depends on confirming the CMS details first.
